title: Which one fails?
examObjective: Converting between output types and data types using DataWeave
prompt: Every script writes `application/xml`. Three produce a document. **One fails.** Which one?

options:
%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ order: { id: 1, name: "A" } }

%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ order: { item: [1, 2] } }

%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ id: 1, name: "A" }

%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ order: null }

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ order: { id: 1, name: "A" } }

explanation.approach: An XML document has exactly one root element. An Object with two top-level keys would need two roots, so the writer refuses. Wrap the fields in one element.

snippets.label: The one that fails
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ id: 1, name: "A" }

snippets.label: One root
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ order: { id: 1, name: "A" } }

snippets.label: An Array becomes repeated elements
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/xml indent=false, writeDeclaration=false
---
{ order: { item: [1, 2] } }
